newsitem.title: FRANCE: Next six months crucial for euro -French minister.
newsitem.headline: Next six months crucial for euro -French minister.

text.p: French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said on Tuesday that Paris will make the final decision whether to join the common European currency once it assesses the state of public finances.
He also said the next six months will be crucial for the future of the single currency.

"We must assess the state of our public finances, and it will be in light of this situation that we will decide whether or not to move to the euro," Moscovici said in an interview on Radio Luxembourg.
"I certainly hope we will do so," he added, but declined to give a clear answer when asked repeatedly whether Paris' entry into the single currency was irrevocable.
"The next six months will be absolutely decisive, and there will be political discussions between the Europeans to decide whether or not we begin the single currency," he said.

France's new Socialist-led government has hailed a European Union pact on jobs, agreed largely at French insistence at the Amsterdam summit on Monday, aimed at putting action for jobs and growth on a par with stringent limits on budget deficits.

Asked whether European states could qualify even if they were above the Maastricht treaty requirement broadly limiting deficits to three percent of gross domestic product, Moscovici said it was possible that a downward trend in deficits could suffice.
